Senior Developer Engineer ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input//` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input//`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["Use the active tracker's dmtools CLI command, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See the dmtools CLI reference section included later in this prompt for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## input_completeness_preflight.md # ⚠️ STEP 0 — INPUT COMPLETENESS PRE-FLIGHT (surface scan, before ANY work) Right after reading the input files, run a QUICK (surface-level) go/no-go scan of the ticket — title, description, and comments authored by humans. Do NOT deep-analyze. Flag only highlights that would force you to ASSUME: - The ticket references an attachment, image, screenshot, logo, design file, or external resource that is NOT present in the ticket context. - Referenced credentials, environment details, or access are missing. - Essential statements contradict each other. If there ARE highlights — do NOT implement. Instead: 1. Post ONE comment on the ticket asking for exactly the missing items. Be specific; propose nothing, assume nothing. If you had already committed work when the missing input surfaced, name the WIP branch (`ai/`) in that comment so the reporter and the next leg know where the partial work lives. 2. Write `outputs/needs-input.md` listing the missing items (same content as the comment). 3. Make NO code changes and stop. The pipeline labels the ticket `ai_questions_asked` and ends the leg without a PR. If there are NO highlights — continue with the normal flow. **Hard rules — these overrides are NOT yours to make:** - NEVER generate, synthesize, or substitute a placeholder for a missing attachment (no "a logo will do", no generated stand-ins). An unattended run is NOT a license to improvise. - NEVER assume a value for missing data "to keep the leg moving". - If missing information surfaces DURING implementation, stop the same way (comment + `outputs/needs-input.md`, no further code changes) instead of guessing. ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Story ticket ready for development]) --> READ_INPUT["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ_INPUT --> PREFLIGHT{"⚠️ STEP 0 input-completeness pre-flight (story legs):

git log, git stash list.
If the fix is genuinely already on the base branch,

'no changes needed' conclusion"] REDO --> IMPLEMENT SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles branch, commit and PR]) ``` ## ⚠️ STEP 0 — INPUT COMPLETENESS PRE-FLIGHT (story legs, before ANY work) Story legs run the STEP 0 input-completeness pre-flight defined in `instructions/common/input_completeness_preflight.md` (it is part of the prompt chain). On this leg the needs-input probe lives in the publish pipeline (`js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js`): a needs-input stop adds the `ai_questions_asked` label and the outcome message names the preserved WIP branch (`ai/`). Before finishing, run the COMPLETION POST-CHECK — see `instructions/common/completion_post_check.md`. ## tdd_approach.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD — Test-Driven Development Workflow"] T0["Start with a clear understanding of the requirement"] T1["RED: Write a failing unit test FIRST
— before any production code
— test must describe the expected behavior
— run it to confirm it FAILS"] T2["GREEN: Write minimum production code to make the test PASS
— no over-engineering
— simplest possible implementation"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up code while keeping tests GREEN
— improve naming, remove duplication
— apply OOP principles
— run tests after every change"] T4{"More requirements to implement?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for next behavior"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All behaviors implemented with tests]) end subgraph RULES["TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER write production code without a failing test first"] R2["❌ NEVER write more production code than needed to pass the test"] R3["✅ Tests must be fast, isolated, and deterministic"] R4["✅ Aim for 100% unit test coverage on new and modified code"] R5["✅ When behavior involves a loop/collection, add a case with 2+ items, not only a single-item happy path — a single-item test can pass while multi-item logic is still wrong"] R6["✅ Run the full test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ## tdd_test_directory.md # TDD Test Directory Rules Write failing unit tests in the repository's existing unit-test tree **only**: - Discover the unit-test directory from the existing build and test configuration and from nearby tests for the code being changed. - Follow the naming, layout, and test-runner conventions already established in that directory. ❌ **Never** place development TDD tests under `testing/`. `testing/` is owned by test-automation agents (regression probes, workflow observation tests, accessibility gates, etc.). If your production changes break existing tests there, leave them untouched and mention the breakage in `outputs/response.md` so the test-automation agent can update them. ## git_completion_guard.md # Git Completion & Closing-Keyword Guard - **Completion guard**: Before writing `outputs/response.md`, run `git fetch origin && git log "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD | cut -d/ -f2)..HEAD" --oneline`. An empty result means your commits did not land — re-do or resume the work before declaring completion. - **No closing keywords in commits or PR bodies**: Do NOT include `Fixes #...`, `Closes #...`, or `Resolves #...` against tracker tickets unless explicitly instructed; ticket lifecycle transitions are managed by the post-action workflow. ## blocked_output_contract.md # Blocked Output Contract (`outputs/blocked.json`) When work cannot proceed because required credentials, secrets, permissions, test data, or external human decisions are missing: 1. Do **not** guess, hardcode, or fake a passing result. 2. Write `outputs/blocked.json` at the repository root with the exact blocker details: ```json { "reason": "Specific external blocker preventing completion", "tried": ["What was checked or attempted"], "needs": "Exact secret, permission, data, or decision a human must provide" } ``` 3. Also write `outputs/response.md` summarizing the blocker so the human sees the explanation in the ticket/PR comment. ## output_rules.md Precondition (including any `"no changes needed"` conclusion): run `git fetch origin && git log "origin/$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref origin/HEAD | cut -d/ -f2)..HEAD" --oneline` per the **Git Completion Guard & Closing-Keyword Rules** section. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/response.md — concise PR description"] O2["Target length: under 20 lines. A reviewer should understand the change in under 30 seconds"] O3["Required sections:
### What changed
1-2 sentences describing the implementation"] O4["### Key decisions
Bullet list of architectural or design choices"] O5["### How to verify
Test command or verification steps"] O6["Optional: add a mermaid diagram inside <details> block summarizing the change"] O7["❌ NO verbose restatement of ticket requirements
❌ NO water words or filler text"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 --> O7 ``` ## completion_post_check.md # ⚠️ COMPLETION POST-CHECK — integration readiness (before finishing) After implementation is done and all tests pass, run a quick integration-readiness scan of YOUR OWN change. Question it answers: **will this feature actually work in the target environment, or does it depend on external setup this repo does not contain?** Flag (as concerns) anything feature-blocking that is NOT code: - External services the code now depends on but that are not provisioned (Firebase, Apple/Google developer config, API backends, databases). - Missing configuration artifacts: `google-services.json`, `GoogleService-Info.plist`, client IDs / API keys / secrets, environment variables, `.entitlements`, URL scheme registrations, Gradle/Info.plist/manifest changes. - Referenced-but-absent external contracts: an endpoint that the provided API spec (e.g. swagger) does not define, a webhook URL that was never registered. **Do NOT flag code-quality, style, architecture, or test-coverage issues — the review agent owns those. Do not duplicate its work.** If there ARE concerns: write `outputs/concerns.md` — for each concern: (a) what the PR does, (b) what is missing, (c) concretely what is needed to make it work (exact file names, IDs, console/account steps). Short and factual; the pipeline appends it to the completion comment and the PR body and labels the ticket `ai_concerns`. If there are NO concerns: write nothing — no file, no label. ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md is a PR description — not a report or essay"] F2["Use bullet points and short sentences, not paragraphs"] F3["Technical focus: WHAT changed and WHY, not WHAT the ticket asked for"] F4["If including mermaid diagram: wrap in <details><summary>Architecture</summary>...</details>"] ``` ## few_shots.md Example PR descriptions — follow this structure and brevity: ```mermaid flowchart TD E1["### What changed
Added JWT validation interceptor to protect all authenticated endpoints."] E2["### Key decisions
- Reused existing `AuthFilter` pattern instead of introducing Spring Security
- Extracted token validation into `JwtValidator` service for testability and reuse"] E3["### How to verify
```bash
./gradlew test --tests '*AuthInterceptorTest*'
```"] E4["<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
REQ[HTTP Request] --> INT[AuthInterceptor]
INT --> VAL[JwtValidator]
VAL -->|valid| CTL[Controller]
VAL -->|invalid| ERR[401 Response]
```

</details>"] ``` ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ## session_ephemerality.md ```mermaid flowchart LR ENV["⚠️ ONE-SHOT SESSION — this agent runs in an ephemeral CI runner.
When your final turn ends, the process EXITS and the runner is destroyed:
- schedule_message / self-reminders NEVER fire after exit — no wake-up exists
- detached processes (nohup/&) are killed with the runner
- nothing can be finished 'later' — there is no later"] ENV --> RULE["NEVER end the session with work pending.
A long job (full test suite, build) must be concluded INSIDE the turn:
run it in background (bash background:true) and poll with
bash_job status/output BETWEEN your steps — the process stays alive
while you keep working — or run it in the foreground if nothing else
remains. Do NOT arm a timer and exit; do NOT nohup-and-exit."] RULE --> ARTIFACT["The ONLY completion artifact is outputs/response.md
written BEFORE you exit. Missing response.md = the run is read as
'interrupted mid-way': the ticket resets for retry and the
whole leg re-runs — your work survives only if committed to the branch."] ``` **Why this matters:** if the agent finishes its edits, launches the full test suite detached (`nohup &`), arms a `schedule_message` wake-up for later, and ends its turn, the process exits code 0, the timer never fires, and `outputs/response.md` is never written — the leg fails with an "interrupted mid-way" reset and burns full runs on an already-completed implementation. ## bash_tools.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SHELLSTATE["⚠️ Persistent-shell pitfalls (sandbox-observed)"] P1["Never end commands with exit — it kills the shell session, making read_bash fail with Invalid shell ID"] P2["Capture the exit code via $? right after the command, before running anything else — a late $? reads the wrong command's code"] P3["Avoid $PIPESTATUS — it produced wrong exit codes in the sandbox; redirect output to a file and check $? instead"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end subgraph BGJOBS["⚠️ Long-running commands — background execution, never foreground-poll"] B1["Any command that can run longer than ~2 minutes (full test suite, coverage run, build, dependency install, dev server or watch mode) MUST be started with bash background: true — you get a job id immediately and the completion notice arrives as a message"] B2["❌ NEVER wait for a long job with foreground sleep-polling: repeated sleep-then-check loops like sleep 540 → ls coverage. A foreground sleep pins the tool-call open — owner steering and cancel cannot reach you until it ends — and burns wall-clock plus a runner slot"] B3["While a background job runs, keep working on other steps — check progress between steps with bash_job status / bash_job output <job-id> — never park the turn in a watch loop"] B4["A harness hint like background candidate: bash background: true, job board /tasks, --wait-for-jobs is an ORDER, not a suggestion — obey it and start the command in the background; working around it with foreground sleeps is a violation"] B5["Verification order: finalize ALL code edits BEFORE launching a long verification run (full suite, coverage) — verification must run against a frozen tree, otherwise the run is wasted"] B6["Files changed while a verification run is in flight? Do NOT kill it mid-flight — let it finish, treat the result as stale, then deliberately start a fresh run against the updated tree"] B7["B6 covers a job still making progress — do NOT kill it mid-flight; a job with NO progress for ~10 min (or 2× its expected duration) is HUNG — dispose of it and MOVE ON: bash_job stop <job-id>, note the disposal in the deliverable (job id, command, last output tail), finish the remaining steps and write outputs/response.md reporting the unverified part. NEVER let a hung child hold the deliverable hostage: validation CI on the pull request is the safety net"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4 --> B5 --> B6 --> B7 end USE --> SHELLSTATE SHELLSTATE --> CWD CWD --> BGJOBS ``` ## development-mode-adaptive-appendix.md # Scope estimate & working mode (adaptive dev leg) Before your FIRST code edit: survey the ticket and the relevant code, then estimate the work and fix your working mode for this leg. ## Estimate - One whole number on an open-ended scale: if the work feels bigger than the value you named, keep going. - Estimate EFFORT, RISK and UNCERTAINTY — not file count. A sweeping mechanical rename is low; a small change into undocumented behavior is high. - Structural surprises belong in a higher estimate: data/schema migrations, changes touching a second repository, unknown integration surfaces. - Uncertainty resolves UP: when torn between two values, take the larger. ## Record Write exactly one JSON object to `outputs//scope_estimate.json` ( = the ticket key): {"sp": , "threshold": , "mode": "plan" | "default", "reason": ""} ## Decide (threshold: 3) - sp >= threshold → work BY A PLAN for the rest of this leg: read `.dmtools/development-mode-plan-appendix.md` now and follow its protocol (numbered tasks with what+verify, the committed snapshot, per-task checkpoints). Never demote back to direct mode within the same leg. - sp < threshold → implement directly; no plan artifacts. - Scope grows mid-work and a re-estimate reaches the threshold → raise it: write plan.md, follow the plan protocol from that point, update the record's "mode" to "plan" (and "sp" to the new estimate). ## Complete honestly Before writing `outputs//response.md`, set the record's final "outcome": "completed" | "blocked". A plan-mode leg reports completion only when its plan tasks are done — or honestly marked blocked/deferred in plan.md. ## github_comment_format.md # GitHub tracker comment Use GitHub-flavored Markdown in `outputs/response.md` for GitHub issue comments and descriptions. Your output is posted to the issue as-is — every construct must render natively on GitHub. - Headings: `##`, `###` - Bullets: `- item` - Numbered lists: `1. item` - Bold: `**text**` - Inline code: `` `code` `` - Code block: ` ```lang ... ``` ` with a language tag (`bash`, `json`, `text`) - Link: `[text](url)` - Tables: standard GFM table syntax (`|---|` separator row) Do not use Jira wiki markup in GitHub fields: no `{code}...{code}` blocks, no `{panel}` macros, no `h1.`/`h2.`/`h3.` heading prefixes, no `{{monospace}}` inline code, no `[title|url]` links. None of it renders on GitHub — a comment full of `{code}` fences and `h3.` headers is unreadable. **IMPORTANT** When the issue references a parent story or related issues, get them for full context using: `dmtools github_get_issue OWNER/REPO#NUMBER` (the composite key form works directly).

You are Fa, a coding agent (also called fa). Never refer to yourself as pi, Claude, or any other assistant name. You help with software engineering tasks in the working directory /home/runner/work/dm_tools_worflow_test_example/dm_tools_worflow_test_example. Use the read, write, ls, and bash tools to inspect and modify files and run commands. Be concise.

## Session recall — never answer about the past from assumption

1. **Reference = search.** When the user references any past decision, rule, task, or artifact ("remember when…", "the rules we made", "that issue from last week"), call `session_search` BEFORE answering. Never answer about the past from assumption.
2. **Resume ritual.** After a compaction boundary is crossed or the session resumes, read the obligations ledger block (the `<system-notice>` titled "obligations ledger") first; it is the contract of what is still owed.
3. **Commit in the open.** Before promising a follow-up, check the ledger. When you arm a timer or watch (`schedule_message`), state the reason clearly in the message text — the engine writes a `pending-wait` ledger entry from it, and the fired timer re-enters a context that knows why it exists.
4. **Durable ≠ session.** Cross-session rules go to long-term memory immediately (`memory_add`); session-scoped obligations stay in the ledger. Never misuse either layer for the other.
5. **Dig idioms.** Markers are the TOC. `session_search` locates, `compact_expand` reads. `read $FAH_SESSION_FILE:<line>` is the zero-tool fallback.

## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
2.5. **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: if the task ships a runnable verifier, test, or entry point the grader will call, run THAT command the way the grader will — neutral cwd (`cd /` — a different working directory, never the session cwd), fresh subprocess, clean env (no session-exported vars) — and compare stdout, stderr, and exit code against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` item to fix before finalizing. The ledger row for the main artifact uses this invocation as its `command:`.
2.6. **Conformance coverage** — applies ONLY when the final claim includes behavioral conformance: "matches the reference/specification", parity with an existing implementation, protocol/format compliance — any domain. Happy-path agreement certifies nothing about rejection paths or option combinations: two implementations agreeing on every well-formed input can still diverge exactly where one of them must say no. A conformance item counts as verified only when the checklist also quotes **negative and combination checks**, each one actually run and quoted in its ledger row: inputs that must be rejected or must error, combinations of incompatible/mutually exclusive options that must be refused, empty and corrupt inputs, boundary values, "must NOT work" / "must not find" cases — alongside the happy paths. A blanket "everything matches" without such coverage is not verified: mark the item `fail` and run the missing cases.
3. **Fix every unmet item** — a failed item is fixed and re-verified. Fix attempts are bounded: don't spiral on one dead end — switch approach.
4. **Final state is the deliverable** — never uninstall, stop, reset, or clean up what you produced while finalizing. Verification steps must be read-only or additive (a smoke probe, a curl, a diff) — never destructive. Cleanup happens only if the task explicitly requires it. ❌ Wrong: "verified, then reset to a clean state so the checker's commands run exactly as written" — the produced state no longer exists at grading, and that is a `fail`, not a clean handoff.

**Feasibility before commitment.** Before starting any step whose cost can dominate the remaining budget (from-source builds, large downloads, brute-force searches), estimate its duration and compare it against the time-left notices. If the estimate exceeds the budget, switch to a cheaper strategy that still satisfies the task (binary packages, targeted sub-builds, reduced scope the task allows) — or, when no satisfying strategy fits, the next-best partial — never gamble the whole window on a path you already know cannot finish.

**Work to the wall.** Your time-left notices report the remaining budget. While work remains, the next compliant action is another approach — not a final answer. Do not stop to wrap up: you are interrupted automatically when time expires, so no manual saving-up is needed. A final answer is written when the task is done or the deadline notice says so.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Archive extraction is complete** — after extracting a provided/downloaded archive into a target directory, diff the archive's full listing against the extracted tree (`unzip -l <archive>` / `tar -tf <archive>` vs `ls -R` of the target, or `find <target> -type f`); every entry — including root-level files with no extension and no obvious purpose (`file_id.diz`, `README`, `LICENSE`, version stamps) — must be present. A partial extraction is a `fail` item.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.netrc`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed). The check runs against the state you leave behind: a file that existed mid-run but is deleted at finalization is a `fail` — final state is the deliverable (step 4).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it before the deadline, reported.

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read the contents of a text file or image. Text output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large text files. Images are returned as base64 content. Video files route to a video-capable model when one is available (the bytes are attached or described with attribution); otherwise a note names how to configure video reading.

## Path selectors

Append a trailing selector to `path` to read exactly the lines you need:

- `:N` — start at line N (1-indexed), through end of file. `:N-` is the same.
- `:A-B` — inclusive line range (`:A..B` works too).
- `:A+C` — C lines starting at A.
- `:R1,R2,…` — multiple ranges, sorted and merged (`:5-16,960-973`); blocks are joined with a `…` separator and ranges past end of file are reported as skipped.
- `:raw` — verbatim content: no line numbers, no hashline header, no notices. Combine as `:raw:50-100` or `:50-100:raw`.

Do not combine `offset`/`limit` with a path selector. Selectors only apply to text files (not images).

## Archives

Read inside `.zip`, `.tar`, `.tar.gz`/`.tgz` files: `archive.zip` lists the root, `archive.zip:dir/` lists a directory, `archive.zip:inner/file.txt` reads a member (selectors apply, e.g. `archive.zip:inner/file.txt:50-60`). Binary members return a note.

## SQLite databases

When the host supports it, `.db`/`.db3`/`.sqlite`/`.sqlite3` paths read as databases: `data.db` lists tables, `data.db:table` shows the schema plus sample rows, `data.db:table:key` fetches one row by primary key (or rowid), `data.db:table?limit=20&offset=40&order=col:desc&where=...` pages a table, and `data.db?q=SELECT ...` runs a raw read-only query.

## Hashline mode

Set hashline=true to prefix lines with line numbers and a [path#TAG] content-hash header for anchoring hashline edit patches (line numbers stay correct on ranged reads). Suppressed by `:raw`.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file, creating parent directories as needed. Overwrites the file if it already exists.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Edit a file in one of two modes.

## Exact-match mode: `path` + `oldText` + `newText`

Replace an exact text occurrence. `oldText` must match exactly (including indentation and newlines) and occur exactly once in the file. Prefer this over `write` for small, precise changes to existing files; read the file first to get the exact text.

## Hashline mode: `patch`

A hashline patch names lines to replace, delete, or insert at by number, bound to a `[PATH#TAG]` content-hash header — precise line addressing without re-quoting file text. To author one, first `read` the file with `hashline=true`: it returns a `[PATH#TAG]` header and `LINE:TEXT` rows. Rule of thumb: a header ending in `:` is followed by `+` body rows; `DEL` has no body.

<headers>
Every file section starts with `[PATH#TAG]`. `TAG` = the 4-hex snapshot tag from your latest hashline `read` or edit response, REQUIRED on every section. Create new files with `write`; hashline only edits existing files. One patch may carry several `[PATH#TAG]` sections (different files); all sections apply or none do.
</headers>

<ops>
`SWAP N.=M:` — replace original lines N.=M with the body rows below. INCLUSIVE — line M is consumed too.
`DEL N.=M` — delete original lines N.=M. No body.
`INS.PRE N:` — insert the body rows immediately before line N.
`INS.POST N:` — insert the body rows immediately after line N.
`INS.HEAD:` / `INS.TAIL:` — insert the body rows at the very start / end of the file.
Single line: `SWAP N.=N:` / `DEL N`. The range is the ORIGINAL lines you touch; body length is irrelevant (replacing 1 line with 10 is still `SWAP N.=N:`).
</ops>

<body-rows>
Body rows appear only under a `:` header. Every body row is `+TEXT` — add a literal line `TEXT`, verbatim (leading whitespace kept); `+` alone adds a blank line. No other row kind. NEVER write `-old` or a bare/context line. To keep a line, leave it out of every range. Literal lines starting with `-`/`+` still need the body prefix: Markdown `- item` → `+- item`, `+ item` → `++ item`.
</body-rows>

<rules>
- Line numbers + `[PATH#TAG]` header come from your latest hashline `read` (`LINE:TEXT` rows) or edit response.
- Numbers refer to the ORIGINAL file; never shift as hunks apply.
- They die with the call: every applied edit mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — anchor the next edit on the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`.
- Touch only lines your latest `read` literally displayed as `LINE:TEXT`; the tag certifies the snapshot, not your memory. A hunk anchored on a line you never displayed is REJECTED — re-`read` that range first.
- Never start or end a range mid-expression or mid-block.
- Indent body rows exactly for the depth they should live at.
- On a stale-tag rejection or any surprising result: STOP and re-`read` before further edits.
- One hunk per range; body = final content, never an old/new pair.
- Ranges cover ONLY lines whose content changes. Never widen over unchanged lines — a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
- Pure additions use `INS.PRE` / `INS.POST` / `INS.HEAD` / `INS.TAIL`, never a widened `SWAP`.
- Non-adjacent changes = separate hunks; untouched lines stay out of every range.
- NEVER format/restyle code with this tool; run the project formatter instead.
</rules>

<example>
Original (the exact shape `read` with `hashline=true` returns):
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
1:def greet(name):
2:    msg = "Hello, " + name
3:    print(msg)
4:greet("world")
```

Insert a guard after line 1:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.POST 1:
+    if not name: name = "stranger"
```

Replace line 2 with two lines:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
SWAP 2.=2:
+    greeting = "Hi"
+    msg = f"{greeting}, {name}"
```

Delete line 3:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
DEL 3
```

Add a header and trailer:
```
[greet.py#A1B2]
INS.HEAD:
+# generated header
INS.TAIL:
+greet("everyone")
```

Insert Markdown bullets — the leading `+` is the body-row marker; the file receives `- task`:
```
[PLAN.md#A1B2]
INS.POST 2:
+- task
+  - nested task
```
</example>

<anti-patterns>
# WRONG — `-` rows / bare context lines do not exist. The range deletes; the body is only the new content.
SWAP 3.=3:
    msg = "Hello, " + name
-   print(msg)
+   return msg
# RIGHT
SWAP 3.=3:
+   return msg

# WRONG — a pure insertion done as a widened `SWAP`: you want to add one line after 2,
# but you replace 2.=4, retype the keepers, and risk dropping one.
SWAP 2.=4:
+    msg = "Hello, " + name
+    extra = compute(name)
+    print(msg)
# RIGHT — touch nothing you keep; the new line is the whole body.
INS.POST 2:
+    extra = compute(name)
</anti-patterns>

<critical>
If you remember nothing else:
1. RE-GROUND AFTER EVERY EDIT. Every apply mints a fresh `#TAG` and renumbers — take the next edit's numbers from the edit response or a fresh hashline `read`. Stale tag or surprise? STOP, re-`read`.
2. RANGES ARE TIGHT. Cover only lines that change; a stale wide range shreds everything it spans.
3. THE BODY IS THE FINAL CONTENT. Every body row starts with `+`; Markdown bullets use `+- item`, not `- item`.
</critical>

tools.name: lsp
tools.description:
Query a language server for diagnostics, navigation, and renames. For Dart/Flutter workspaces the Dart analysis server (`dart language-server`) starts automatically on first use; other servers can be added via `.fah/lsp.json`.

## Ops

- `diagnostics {path}` — analyzer errors/warnings for a file. Returns `OK` when clean.
- `definition {path, line, character}` — where the symbol at the position is defined.
- `references {path, line, character}` — every reference to the symbol at the position.
- `rename {path, line, character, newName}` — rename the symbol at the position workspace-wide. The server's workspace edit is applied atomically, so barrel files and imports update together; per-file edit counts are reported.

`line` and `character` are 1-indexed and default to 1.

## Rules

- Prefer this over `bash dart analyze` for a single file; diagnostics come back scoped and severity-sorted.
- Prefer `rename` over manual search-and-replace for identifiers: the analysis server finds every reference, including exports and imports.
- Positions point at the symbol's first letter. When unsure of the exact column, `read` the line first.
- Definition/references results render as `file:line:col` with the source line; follow up with `read` for more context.
- If no server is configured for a file type, add one to `.fah/lsp.json` (servers map with `command`, `args`, `fileTypes`, `rootMarkers`).

tools.name: memory_add
tools.description:
# `memory_add` policy

## What to store

Store only **durable** facts — things that must survive across sessions:

- project conventions, architecture decisions and their rationale;
- user preferences, habits, environment facts;
- key discoveries that were expensive to learn (non-obvious behaviour,
  gotchas, working configurations).

Do **not** store task progress, transient state, or anything derivable
from the repository itself (file contents, git history, current diffs).

## The supersede rule

Facts age. When a problem is **solved** or a fact **changes**:

1. delete the outdated record (`memory_delete` by id or exact text —
   deletions are tombstoned, so the old text cannot be re-captured);
2. add the new fact as a fresh record.

Never leave temporary difficulties, workarounds, or "currently broken"
notes in memory forever. A memory full of solved problems actively
misleads future sessions. If you used a record to fix something, that
record's job is done — supersede it.

Before adding anything, `memory_search` for an existing record on the
topic: update (delete + add) instead of duplicating.

## Scope discipline

- **project scope** (default) lives in the project's memory directory and
  is **public**: it is committed to git and shared with everyone who
  clones the repository. Never store secrets, credentials, personal data,
  or anything you would not put in a public commit message.
- **user scope** is global and private to the user's machine. Use it for
  cross-project preferences and facts about the user.

## Style

- One fact per record, concise and self-contained (readable without the
  conversation that produced it).
- Add concrete tags (see [tag_taxonomy.md](tag_taxonomy.md)).
- Prefer facts with staying power: "tests run with `--exclude-tags
  integration`" outlives "I am currently fixing the test suite".

Deliver your explicit answer to the parent agent. Call this when your task output is ready — the text becomes the parent-visible reply. If you never call it, the parent still sees your final message as a completion notice, but an explicit reply is the reliable channel.

REPORT SIZE: per-message budget 8000 chars — you may send one complete reply even when it is larger: the harness auto-spills it (the full text is stored as an agent:// artifact; the parent gets an excerpt + pointer + completeness, and this tool result names the reference). Manual chunking (ordered agent_message parts with report_id + 0-based part_index, more=false on the last, then a final manifest reply carrying report_id + report_parts) is the FALLBACK for when auto-spill is unavailable. See REPORT SIZE CONTRACT in your system prompt. Never probe the output limit.

# CI Heal — the self-heal kicker (spec: audit/self-heal-kicker-spec, layer H).
# Probe MONITORED workflows; sickness = the latest FAIL_STREAK runs ALL failed
# (consecutive — any green/cancel resets the streak; stale reds never re-fire
# after a fix: branch-protection "latest run is the verdict" semantics).
# Dedup: one incident = one issue — a workflow already covered by an OPEN
# issue labeled wf:<name> is skipped, so a broken shared key does not spawn
# five issues. Uncovered sick workflows go to the ci_analyst agent pack
# (.dmtools/packs/ci_analyst-*.zip via runners/fa-analyst.json), which files
# ONE issue labeled ci-heal + wf:<name> + agent:dev — the machine loop then
# fixes it like any other issue and machine-merge closes it on the fix PR.
name: 'CI Heal'

on:
  workflow_dispatch: {}
  schedule:
    # A4: every 30 minutes (UTC). Healthy state costs nothing — the probe is
    # read-only gh queries; the analyst/legs fire only on live incidents.
    - cron: '*/30 * * * *' 

permissions:
  actions: read
  issues: write
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-heal
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # MONITORED is auto-discovered by the "Discover monitored workflows" step:
  # every repo workflow except ci-heal itself and the LEG lanes below.
  # HEAL_ALLOW_MONITORED non-empty = probe ONLY that explicit list.
  HEAL_ALLOW_MONITORED: ''
  # Exclude-list: workflow FILENAMES or names, space-separated.
  HEAL_EXCLUDE_MONITORED: 'ci-heal.yml' 
  # Parameterized factory-owned legs (group-key lanes; see run-name contract
  # in the Run-name scan step below).
  LEG_WORKFLOWS: |
    AI Teammate
    Params Drill
    Geo Probe
  # Sickness threshold: N CONSECUTIVE latest failures.
  FAIL_STREAK: '2'
  # Failing-job log tail per run handed to the analyst.
  LOG_TAIL_LINES: '200'

jobs:
  heal:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: Checkout (for .dmtools/config.js machineAuthor)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: 'Discover monitored workflows (default = all but ci-heal + legs)'
        id: discover
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          ALLOW="$(echo "${HEAL_ALLOW_MONITORED}" | xargs)"
          if [ -n "$ALLOW" ]; then
            echo "allow-list set — probing only: $ALLOW"
            echo "monitored=$ALLOW" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          LEGS="$(echo "${LEG_WORKFLOWS}" | tr '\n' ' ' | xargs)"
          LIST=""
          for F in .github/workflows/*.y*ml; do
            [ -e "$F" ] || continue
            BASE=$(basename "$F")
            # Keys are FILENAMES — the stable unit identity (space-free, so
            # the space-separated list survives; gh resolves filenames fine).
            case " $HEAL_EXCLUDE_MONITORED " in *" $BASE "*) continue ;; esac
            # LEG lanes are watched by the per-parameter group detector,
            # not by the same-head streak probe — keep them out of MONITORED.
            # Match LEG entries against both the filename and the name: field
            # (LEG_WORKFLOWS is name-based, the run-name contract scans it).
            NAME=$(awk -F': ' '/^name:/{print $2; exit}' "$F" | sed "s/^['\"]//; s/['\"]\$//")
            case " $LEGS " in *" $BASE "*|*" $NAME "*) continue ;; esac
            LIST="$LIST $BASE"
          done
          LIST="$(echo "$LIST" | xargs)"
          echo "monitored discovered: $LIST"
          echo "monitored=$LIST" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Probe monitored workflows (2 consecutive reds = sick)
        id: probe
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          MONITORED: ${{ steps.discover.outputs.monitored }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          SICK=""
          mkdir -p /tmp/heal
          for WF in $MONITORED; do
            # Probe the DEFAULT branch only: a green run from a PR head must
            # never mask main's red streak (branch-protection semantics).
            DATA=$(gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow "$WF" -L "$FAIL_STREAK" \
                     --branch main \
                     --json databaseId,conclusion,headSha,displayTitle,url)

            if [ "$CNT" -lt "$FAIL_STREAK" ]; then
              echo "$WF: only $CNT run(s) — not enough history, skip"
              continue
            fi
            FAILS=$(echo "$DATA" | jq '[.[] | select(.conclusion=="failure" or .conclusion=="timed_out")] | length')
            if [ "$FAILS" -eq "$FAIL_STREAK" ]; then
              # Streak must live on the CURRENT head: reds on a stale sha are
              # not an incident — main already moved, the fresh run will tell.
              HEAD=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/main" --jq '.sha')
              TOPSHA=$(echo "$DATA" | jq -r '.[0].headSha')
              if [ "$TOPSHA" != "$HEAD" ]; then
                echo "$WF: reds are on stale sha ${TOPSHA:0:8}, head is ${HEAD:0:8} — verdict pending fresh run, skip"
                continue
              fi
              echo "$WF: SICK ($FAILS/$FAIL_STREAK consecutive red on head ${TOPSHA:0:8})"
              SICK="$SICK $WF"
              echo "$DATA" | jq -c '.[]' > "/tmp/heal/runs-${WF//\//-}.jsonl"
            else
              echo "$WF: healthy (streak reset — latest green or mixed window)"
            fi
          done
          SICK="$(echo $SICK | xargs)"   # trim
          echo "sick=$SICK" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ -z "$SICK" ]; then
            echo "✅ all monitored workflows healthy — sleeping"
          fi

      - name: Ensure heal labels exist
        if: steps.probe.outputs.sick != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh label create ci-heal -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --color D93F0B \
            --description "Self-heal analyst issue" 2>/dev/null || true
          for WF in ${{ steps.probe.outputs.sick }}; do
            gh label create "wf:$WF" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --color BFD4F2 \
              --description "Affected workflow: $WF" 2>/dev/null || true
          done

      - name: Dedup — drop workflows already covered by an open heal issue
        id: dedup
        if: steps.probe.outputs.sick != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          UNCOVERED=""
          for WF in ${{ steps.probe.outputs.sick }}; do
            OPEN=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label "wf:$WF" --state open \
                     --json number --jq 'length')
            if [ "$OPEN" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$WF: already covered by an open heal issue — skip"
            else
              UNCOVERED="$UNCOVERED $WF"
            fi
          done
          UNCOVERED="$(echo $UNCOVERED | xargs)"
          echo "uncovered=$UNCOVERED" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ -z "$UNCOVERED" ]; then
            echo "✅ every sick workflow has an open heal issue — nothing to file"
          fi

      - name: Anchor gate — closed heal-issues make their reds history
        id: anchors
        if: steps.dedup.outputs.uncovered != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          TODO=""
          : > /tmp/heal/prev.jsonl
          for WF in ${{ steps.dedup.outputs.uncovered }}; do
            CISS=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label "wf:$WF" --label ci-heal \
                     --state closed --limit 1 --json number,title,closedAt --jq '.[0]' || true)
            if [ -z "$CISS" ]; then
              TODO="$TODO $WF"; continue
            fi
            NUM=$(jq -r '.number' <<<"$CISS")
            # Closure commit: the state anchor (v2.3). Native "Closes" closes
            # record commit_id; API closures leave it null — fall back to the
            # merged fix PR of the dev leg's branch (verified live on #9).
            CC=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/issues/$NUM/timeline" \
                   --jq '[.[] | select(.event=="closed") | .commit_id][0]' 2>/dev/null || true)
            if [ -z "$CC" ] || [ "$CC" = "null" ]; then
              CC=$(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state merged --head "ai/gh-$NUM" \
                     --json mergeCommit --jq '.[0].mergeCommit.oid' 2>/dev/null || true)
            fi
            if [ -z "$CC" ] || [ "$CC" = "null" ]; then
              echo "$WF: closed issue #$NUM has no knowable closure commit — treat as fresh"
              TODO="$TODO $WF"; continue
            fi
            # SHA order is meaningless — freshness is ancestry (compare API):
            # behind|identical = reds are the incident's own history; a red
            # ahead|diverged of the closure is a fresh world.
            FRESH=0
            for FS in $(jq -r 'select(.conclusion=="failure" or .conclusion=="timed_out") | .sha' \
                        "/tmp/heal/runs-${WF//\//-}.jsonl" | sort -u); do
              # Fresh = NOT behind: a red AT the closure commit is the
              # "fix ineffective" case (v2.1 Q2) — re-analyze, never skip.
              ST=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/compare/$CC...$FS" --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
              case "$ST" in behind) : ;; *) FRESH=1;; esac
            done
            if [ "$FRESH" -eq 1 ]; then
              echo "$WF: reds are newer than the closure of #$NUM — fresh incident"
              TODO="$TODO $WF"
              jq -c --arg sha "$CC" \
                '{issue:.number,title:.title,closedAt:.closedAt,closedByCommit:$sha}' \
                <<<"$CISS" >> /tmp/heal/prev.jsonl
            else
              echo "$WF: reds are at/before the closure of #$NUM — incident history, skip"
            fi
          done
          TODO="$(echo $TODO | xargs)"
          echo "todo=$TODO" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "prev=$(jq -sc . /tmp/heal/prev.jsonl)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ -z "$TODO" ]; then
            echo "✅ every sick workflow is covered by a closure anchor — sleeping"
          fi

      - name: Run-name contract scan (factory repairs its own observability)
        id: runame
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euxo pipefail
          mkdir -p /tmp/heal
          NONCONFORM=""
          while IFS= read -r WF; do
            FILE=$(grep -rl "^name: ['\"]\?$WF['\"]\?$" .github/workflows/ 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
            if [ -z "$FILE" ]; then
              echo "$WF: workflow file not found - skip"; continue
            fi
            PARAM=$(grep -qE "inputs:|issues:" "$FILE" && echo yes || echo no)
            RN=$(awk '/^run-name:/{f=1} f' "$FILE" | head -20)
            if [ -z "$RN" ]; then
              if [ "$PARAM" = "yes" ]; then NONCONFORM="$NONCONFORM $WF"; echo "$WF: parameterized but NO run-name"; continue
              else echo "$WF: no run-name, not parameterized - ok"; continue; fi
            fi
            # First-token rule: SOME quoted template must hold a placeholder
            # ('{') whose literal prefix is empty or a short stable tag (gh-,
            # pr-, param-), and the run-name must not embed run-varying values.
            # (The first quote in an expression is often a comparison operand
            # like '' - literals without '{' are skipped.)
            CAND=0
            for LIT in $(printf '%s' "$RN" | grep -oE "'[^']*'" | sed "s/^'//; s/'$//"); do
              case "$LIT" in *'{'*)
                PREFIX=$(printf '%s' "$LIT" | sed 's/[{$].*//' | tr -d '[:space:]')
                printf '%s' "$PREFIX" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,6}$' && CAND=1
                break
              ;; esac
            done
            NOISE=$(printf '%s' "$RN" | grep -icE "run_id|run_number|timestamp|head_sha" || true)
            if [ "$PARAM" = "yes" ] && [ "$CAND" -eq 0 ]; then
              NONCONFORM="$NONCONFORM $WF"
              echo "$WF: parameterized, no leading group template found - group hidden"
            elif [ "$NOISE" -gt 0 ]; then
              NONCONFORM="$NONCONFORM $WF"
              echo "$WF: group token contains run-varying values - unstable key"
            else
              echo "$WF: run-name contract ok (param=$PARAM)"
            fi
          done <<< "$LEG_WORKFLOWS"
          echo "scan: loop finished"

          NONCONFORM="$(printf '%s' "$NONCONFORM" | xargs -r || true)"
          printf 'nonconform=%s\n' "$NONCONFORM" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "scan: nonconform=[$NONCONFORM]"
          if [ -n "$NONCONFORM" ]; then
            MA="$(sed -nE "s/.*machineAuthor:[[:space:]]*'([^']+)'.*/\1/p" .dmtools/config.js | head -1)"
            DEDUP=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label run-name-fix --state open --json number --jq 'length')
            if [ "$DEDUP" -eq 0 ]; then
              gh label create run-name-fix -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --color FBCA04 2>/dev/null || true
              {
                echo '**Run-name contract** (self-heal observability): for every parameterized factory-owned workflow, the `run-name` FIRST token must be the stable group key - it must contain the dispatch parameter (`inputs.*` / issue number) and must NOT contain run-varying values (`run_id`, `run_number`, timestamps, SHAs).'
                echo ''
                echo "**Non-conforming:** $NONCONFORM"
                echo ''
                echo '**Fix:** restructure the `run-name` so the group token leads, e.g. `run-name: gh-${{ inputs.issue }} - dev` for an issue-parameterized leg. Plain (non-parameterized) workflows may use the workflow name as the token.'
                echo ''
                echo '**Why:** the self-heal legs-health detector groups runs by the first run-name token; without a leading group token a chronically failing parameter is invisible (interleaved greens reset raw streaks). The fix must ONLY adjust `run-name` - no behavioral changes. Use `Closes #<this issue>`.'
              } > /tmp/heal/body.md
              gh issue create -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
                --title "[ci-heal] run-name contract: group token must lead the run-name" \
                --label "ci-heal,run-name-fix,agent:dev" \
                ${MA:+--assignee "$MA"} \
                --body-file /tmp/heal/body.md 2>&1 | tail -1 || echo '::warning::run-name-fix issue creation failed - will retry next tick'
            else
              echo "run-name-fix issue already open - skip filing"
            fi
          fi
          echo "scan: step complete"
          exit 0

      - name: Legs health - per-group 2-failures detector (collect for analyst)
        id: legs
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p /tmp/heal
          : > /tmp/heal/leg-runs.jsonl
          FOUND=false
          # Freshness guard, PER-WORKFLOW: only runs dispatched AFTER the last
          # commit that touched THIS lane's own workflow file count as live
          # evidence. A global CUT let unrelated merges bury a lane's signal
          # (the Geo Probe startup-failure case): each lane's fix lives in its
          # own file, so its own file's last-commit time is the honest anchor.
          while IFS= read -r WF; do
            WFFILE=$(grep -rl "^name: ['\"]\?$WF['\"]\?$" .github/workflows/ 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)
            # shallow checkout (depth=1) makes `git log -1 -- path` return HEAD
            # for ANY path, so CUT would always be "now" and every run would be
            # stale. Use the commits API - it sees the real file history.
            CUT=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits?path=${WFFILE}&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].commit.committer.date | sub("[.][0-9]+"; "") | fromdateiso8601' 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
            [ -z "$CUT" ] && CUT=0
            echo "lane=$WF wffile=${WFFILE:-NONE} cut=${CUT:-EMPTY}"
            gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow "$WF" -L 10 --json databaseId,displayTitle,conclusion,createdAt > /tmp/heal/legs-raw.json || true
            echo "raw top3: $(jq -c 'map([.conclusion, (.displayTitle | .[0:24]), .createdAt | if type == "string" then .[11:19] else . end])' /tmp/heal/legs-raw.json 2>/dev/null || echo ERR)"
            JQPROG='map(select(((.createdAt | sub("[.][0-9]+"; "") | fromdateiso8601)) > '"$CUT"')) | map(select(.conclusion != null and .conclusion != "")) | map({key: (if (.displayTitle | startswith("Merge pull request")) and (.conclusion == "failure") then "startup" else (.displayTitle | split(" ")[0]) end), conclusion: (.conclusion // "running"), url: .url, id: .databaseId}) | sort_by(.key) | group_by(.key) | .[] | select((.[0].conclusion == "failure") and ((.[1].conclusion == "failure") or .[0].key == "startup")) | .[0].key + "\t" + ([.[] | select(.conclusion == "failure")] | map(.id | tostring) | join(","))'
            gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow "$WF" -L 10 \
              --json databaseId,displayTitle,conclusion,url,createdAt \
              --jq "$JQPROG" \
              > /tmp/heal/legs-sick.txt || echo '::warning::legs jq failed - see log above'
            echo "legs-sick.txt lines: $(wc -l < /tmp/heal/legs-sick.txt | tr -d ' ') | content: $(cat /tmp/heal/legs-sick.txt | tr '\n' '; ')"
            while IFS=$'\t' read -r KEY IDS; do
              [ -z "$KEY" ] && continue
              OPEN=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label ci-heal --state open \
                       --json number,body --jq "[.[] | select((.body // \"\") | contains(\"$KEY\"))] | length")
              if [ "$OPEN" -gt 0 ]; then
                echo "$WF [$KEY]: already covered by an open heal issue - skip"; continue
              fi
              echo "$WF [$KEY]: 2 consecutive group failures - handing to analyst"
              FOUND=true
              for RID in $(echo "$IDS" | tr ',' ' '); do
                TAIL=$(gh run view "$RID" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --log-failed 2>/dev/null | tail -n 120 || echo "(log unavailable)")
                TAIL_JSON=$(printf '%s' "$TAIL" | jq -Rs .)
                jq -cn --arg wf "leg: $WF group $KEY" --arg url \
                  "https://github.com/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/$RID" \
                  --arg sha "$RID" --arg log "$TAIL_JSON" \
                  '{workflow:$wf, url:$url, sha:$sha, conclusion:"failure", logTail:($log | fromjson)}' \
                  >> /tmp/heal/leg-runs.jsonl
              done
            done < /tmp/heal/legs-sick.txt
          done <<< "$LEG_WORKFLOWS"
          echo "found=$FOUND" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Build analyst context (JSON per ci_analyst contract)
        id: context
        if: steps.anchors.outputs.todo != '' || steps.legs.outputs.found == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PREV: ${{ steps.anchors.outputs.prev }}
          LEGS: ${{ steps.legs.outputs.found }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MA="$(sed -nE "s/.*machineAuthor:[[:space:]]*'([^']+)'.*/\1/p" .dmtools/config.js | head -1)"
          if [ -z "$MA" ]; then
            echo "::warning::machineAuthor not found in .dmtools/config.js — analyst will skip issue assignment"
          fi
          echo "machineAuthor=$MA" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          : > /tmp/heal/ctx-runs.jsonl
          for WF in ${{ steps.anchors.outputs.todo }}; do
            FILE="/tmp/heal/runs-${WF//\//-}.jsonl"
            while IFS= read -r ROW; do
              RID=$(jq -r '.databaseId' <<<"$ROW")
              CONC=$(jq -r '.conclusion' <<<"$ROW")
              LOG=""
              if [ "$CONC" = "failure" ] || [ "$CONC" = "timed_out" ]; then
                LOG=$(gh run view "$RID" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --log-failed 2>/dev/null \
                        | tail -n "$LOG_TAIL_LINES" || echo "(log unavailable)")
              fi
              jq -cn --argjson row "$ROW" --arg wf "$WF" --arg log "$LOG" \
                '{workflow:$wf, url:$row.url, sha:$row.headSha, conclusion:$row.conclusion, logTail:$log}' \
                >> /tmp/heal/ctx-runs.jsonl
            done < "$FILE"
          done
          TODO='${{ steps.anchors.outputs.todo }}'
          WFS='[]'
          [ -n "$TODO" ] && WFS=$(echo "$TODO" | tr ' ' '\n' | jq -R . | jq -s -c .) || true
          RUNS=$(jq -s '.' /tmp/heal/ctx-runs.jsonl /tmp/heal/leg-runs.jsonl) || RUNS='[]'
          OPENI=$(gh issue list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --label ci-heal --state open \
                    --json number,title,createdAt,labels \
                    --jq '[.[] | {number: .number, title: .title, createdAt: .createdAt, workflows: ([.labels[]? | select(.name | startswith("wf:")) | .name[3:]])}]') || OPENI='[]'
          # B3-lite: per-workflow outcome counts over the recent window —
          # the analyst weighs failure rates for systemic suspicion.
          STATS='['
          FIRST=1
          for SWF in $(echo "${MONITORED:-}" "$LEG_WORKFLOWS" | tr '\n' ' ' | xargs); do
            S=$(gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow "$SWF" -L 10 --json conclusion \
                  --jq '{workflow: "'"$SWF"'", window: length, failures: ([.[] | select(.conclusion=="failure" or .conclusion=="timed_out")] | length), greens: ([.[] | select(.conclusion=="success")] | length)}' 2>/dev/null || true)
            [ -z "$S" ] && continue
            if [ "$FIRST" -eq 1 ]; then STATS="$STATS$S"; FIRST=0; else STATS="$STATS,$S"; fi
          done
          STATS="$STATS]"
          jq -n --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --arg ma "$MA" \
                --argjson wfs "$WFS" --argjson runs "$RUNS" \
                --argjson prev "${PREV:-[]}" --argjson openIncidents "${OPENI:-[]}" \
                --argjson workflowStats "${STATS:-[]}" \
                '{targetRepository:$repo, machineAuthor:$ma, dryRun:false,
                  monitoredWorkflows:$wfs, runs:$runs, previousIncidents:$prev, openIncidents:$openIncidents, workflowStats:$workflowStats}' > heal-context.json
          jq -c 'del(.runs[].logTail)' heal-context.json   # shape check, sans logs

      - name: Install factory kit + CLIs (dmtools, fa)
        if: steps.anchors.outputs.todo != '' || steps.legs.outputs.found == 'true'
        env:
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          # PAT, not github.token: fa ships from the PRIVATE harness repo —
          # github.token cannot even list its releases (silent asset-less).
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          DMTOOLS_VERSION: latest
          FA_VERSION: latest
          DMTOOLS_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          KIT="$RUNNER_TEMP/factory-kit"
          git init -q "$KIT"
          git -C "$KIT" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows
          git -C "$KIT" fetch -q --depth 1 origin main
          git -C "$KIT" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
          if [ "${DMTOOLS_VERSION}" = "latest" ]; then
            # GITHUB_ENV writes only reach LATER steps — resolve inline instead
            export DMTOOLS_VERSION="$(gh release view --repo epam/dmtools-dart --json tagName --jq .tagName)"
            echo "dmtools CLI: latest resolved to ${DMTOOLS_VERSION}"
          fi
          # FACTORY_ROOT: the agents repo's setup/ tree — install-fa-cli.sh
          # dispatches setup/install.sh "fa:<ver>" through it at the end.
          AG="$RUNNER_TEMP/dmtools-agents"
          git init -q "$AG"
          git -C "$AG" remote add origin https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents
          git -C "$AG" fetch -q --depth 1 origin main
          git -C "$AG" sparse-checkout set setup
          git -C "$AG" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
          export FACTORY_ROOT="$AG"
          bash "$KIT/scripts/install-dmtools-cli.sh"
          bash "$KIT/scripts/install-fa-cli.sh"
          echo "$HOME/.dmtools/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Run ci_analyst agent pack
        if: steps.anchors.outputs.todo != '' || steps.legs.outputs.found == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ZAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_API_KEY || secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
          AI_AGENT_PROVIDER: fa
          DEFAULT_TRACKER: github
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MA="${{ steps.context.outputs.machineAuthor }}"
          WFLIST=$(echo ${{ steps.anchors.outputs.todo }} | tr ' ' ',')
          mkdir -p input
          {
            echo "[ci-heal] $WFLIST: failing"
            echo
            echo "Analyze the failing CI runs described in heal-context.json."
            echo "Classify adequate vs noise (SHA-aware: stale reds under a fresh green are noise)."
            echo "Print the STRICT JSON verdict; if adequate, create ONE heal issue per the ci_analyst contract."
            echo "dryRun=false."
          } > input/ticket.md
          CONTEXT_ID="ci-heal-${{ github.run_id }}"
          dmtools run .dmtools/runners/fa-analyst.json \
            --metadata "{\"contextId\":\"$CONTEXT_ID\"}" \
            --customParams "{\"contextPath\":\"heal-context.json\",\"dryRun\":false,\"machineAuthor\":\"$MA\",\"targetRepository\":\"$GITHUB_REPOSITORY\"}"

      - name: Surface the verdict in the run summary
        if: steps.anchors.outputs.todo != '' || steps.legs.outputs.found == 'true'
        run: |
          {
            if [ -f outputs/ci_analyst_result.json ]; then
              echo '### ci_analyst result'
              echo '```json'
              cat outputs/ci_analyst_result.json
              echo '```'
            fi
            if [ -f outputs/response.md ]; then
              echo '### analyst response'
              cat outputs/response.md
            fi
            [ -f outputs/response.md ] || [ -f outputs/ci_analyst_result.json ] || \
              echo "_analyst produced no outputs_"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  cancel-in-progress: true

- A test pins the env fallback equal to the workflow_dispatch default so the two definitions cannot drift.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test --reporter expanded
```
